DLMF 18.17.21; classical Hilb and interior Legendre asymptotics
correctness.rationale: The sine transform at frequency 2r has squared norm pi/4 times the input squared norm; squaring the DLMF identity then gives I_k=(1/pi) integral_0^1 P_k(1-2x^2)^2 dx, including k=0. Direct polynomial integration gives 1, 7/15, 11/35 for pi I_0, pi I_1 and pi I_2. For the tail, put K=k+1/2 and Q_k=pi I_k. In the low-angle integral for 2KQ_k, Hilb's errors O(theta^2) for theta<=1/K and O(theta^(1/2)K^(-3/2)) beyond give o(1) after squaring and integrating with the K factor. The amplitude factor theta/(2 sin(theta/2)) contributes an O(delta^2) error by J_0(u)^2=O((1+u)^(-1)). On [delta,pi-epsilon], interior cosine asymptotics give oscillatory averaging; the Bernstein bound makes the omitted right strip O(epsilon) uniformly since cos(theta/2)/sin(theta)=1/(2 sin(theta/2)). The complementary integral thus contributes log cot(delta/4)/pi. The Laplace transform of J_0^2 is (1/pi) integral_0^(pi/2) [(s/2)^2+sin^2 u]^(-1/2)du, asymptotic to log(8/s)/pi; subtracting the model kernel [(s/2)^2+u^2]^(-1/2) gives the constant. Integration by parts of the primitive transfers this to (log T+gamma+log 8)/pi+o(1) for the primitive at T. Matching at fixed delta and then letting delta tend to zero adds log 4, giving gamma+log 32. Xu's normalization and exponent produce the displayed coefficient from I_0 and I_1. The derivation, rather than the frozen finite quadratures, establishes the infinite claims.
residual_risks: The proof gives o(K^(-1)), not an effective uniform remainder bound. The frozen verification script was not rerun.
